name: Princeton University
essay_req_en: 3 required essays (academic interests 250 words; lived experience/community 400-500 words; service & civic engagement 250 words) + 3 short answers (50 words each) — same as last year.

name: Massachusetts Institute of Technology
essay_req_en: 4 required essays (100-200 words each) + 4 required short answers (40-50 words each).
essay_change_en: Cut essays from 5 to 4 (collaboration prompt dropped) and added 4 new 40-50-word short answers (what you do for fun, someone you admire, a topic you could talk about for hours, generalist/specialist) — 'what you do for fun' reduced from a 150-word essay to a short answer.

name: Harvard University
essay_req_en: 5 required short answers (150 words each: contribution, an experience of disagreement, activities/responsibilities, how you plan to use your Harvard education, 3 things to tell your roommate) — same as last year.

name: Stanford University
essay_req_en: 5 required short questions (max 50 words each) + 3 short essays (100-250 words each: excitement for learning, a note to your roommate, what you would contribute to Stanford) — same as last year.

name: Yale University
essay_req_en: Select academic areas + academic interest essay (200 words) + 3 Short Takes (200 characters each) + one 400-word essay (choose 1 of 3 prompts).
essay_change_en: Dropped the 'Why Yale' (125 words) question and reduced Short Takes from 4 to 3 (200 characters each).

name: University of Chicago
essay_req_en: 2 required: 'Why UChicago' + 1 extended (Uncommon) essay (choose 1 of 6 options) — same structure; only the option topics rotate annually, as in past years.
merit_note_en: UChicago Merit Scholarships (automatic consideration for all first-year applicants; no separate application)

name: Duke University
essay_req_en: 2 required essays (Why Duke 250 words + community 250 words) + up to 1 of 3 optional prompts (250 words).
essay_change_en: Required essays expanded from 1 to 2 (community prompt made required), optional prompts cut from 5 to 3 (respond to at most 1), and the AI-related optional prompt introduced last cycle dropped after just one year.
merit_note_en: A.B. Duke Memorial Scholarship, Robertson Scholars Leadership Program (Duke-administered merit: no separate application; Robertson requires its own application)

name: Johns Hopkins University
essay_req_en: 1 required essay (350 words): prompt on engaging across differences, bridge building, and community.
essay_change_en: Still a single essay, but the topic changed — from the 150th-anniversary 'important first' prompt (an important first experience in your life) to a prompt on dialogue across differences and bridge building.

name: Northwestern University
essay_req_en: 1 required short answer (300 words, how your background will shape your engagement in the Northwestern community) + up to 2 of 5 optional prompts (200 words each); the Common App personal essay is now optional.
essay_change_en: Replaced the required 'Why Northwestern' question with a background/community engagement prompt, and made the Common App personal essay optional instead of required (essays written for other applications may be reused).

name: University of Pennsylvania
essay_req_en: 3 required (150-200 words each): thank-you note, community, and a school-specific prompt + additional essays for dual-degree/specialized programs — same as last year.

name: California Institute of Technology (Caltech)
essay_req_en: 5 required responses (two-part area-of-interest prompt 150-200 words; 1 of 2 'scholarly attitude' prompts 200 words; 2 of 3 'scientific inquiry' prompts 200 words each; a fun community-contribution prompt 100-150 words) + 1 optional (explaining academic context).
essay_change_en: Full prompt overhaul — dropped the previous prompts on how you discovered your STEM interest and on creativity (creator/inventor), introduced a choice-based structure (1 of 2, 2 of 3), and added a step to confirm the guidelines on ethical AI use before submission.

name: Cornell University
essay_req_en: No university-wide essay — only college-specific essays (e.g., Arts & Sciences one 650-word essay, CALS two 350-word essays, Engineering 2 essays + 4 short answers).
essay_change_en: Dropped the community essay (350 words) previously required of all applicants, leaving only college-specific essays; CALS changed from one 500-word essay to two 350-word essays.

name: Brown University
essay_req_en: 4 required essays: Open Curriculum (150-250 words), upbringing/background and contribution (150-250 words), a class you would like to teach (100-150 words), what brings you joy (100-150 words).
essay_change_en: Supplement overhaul — dropped the short-answer section (3-word self-description, one-sentence Why Brown, etc.) from the previous '3 essays + short answers' format and added a newly written Open Curriculum prompt, moving to a 4-essay format.

name: Dartmouth College
essay_req_en: 3 required essays: Why Dartmouth 100 words + two 250-word essays (choose 1 from 2 options and 1 from 6 options, respectively). Same structure for the last two cycles; only some option prompts replaced.

name: Columbia University
essay_req_en: 1 list question (texts/resources that contributed to your intellectual growth, 100 words) + 5 short answers of 150 words (lived experience, an experience of disagreement, overcoming adversity, Why Columbia, major interest). Same set kept since the 2023-24 overhaul.

name: University of California, Berkeley
essay_req_en: UC application PIQs: choose 4 of 8 questions, 350 words max each. No change in number or policy for Fall 2027 applicants (2026-27 cycle).
merit_note_en: Regents' and Chancellor's Scholarship (automatic consideration for all applicants incl. international first-years)

name: Rice University
essay_req_en: 3 required essays (major interest 150 words + Rice experience 150 words + one 500-word essay, choose 1: residential college contribution or change agent) + image upload 'The Box'. Same structure for the last two cycles.
merit_note_en: Merit scholarships incl. Trustee Distinguished Scholarship; all admitted first-years automatically considered, no separate application

name: University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA)
essay_req_en: UC application PIQs: choose 4 of 8 questions, 350 words max each. No change in number or policy for Fall 2027 applicants (2026-27 cycle).

name: Vanderbilt University
essay_req_en: 1 required short answer (~250 words): prompt built on the motto 'Crescere aude (dare to grow)', asking how your identity/culture/background shaped your growth and how you would contribute to campus. Unchanged for 2026-27.
essay_change_en: In the 2025-26 cycle, dropped the long-used extracurricular description prompt and replaced it with the 'Crescere aude' identity/growth prompt (still 1 essay).
merit_note_en: Cornelius Vanderbilt Scholarship, Ingram Scholars Program (signature full-tuition merit awards)

name: Carnegie Mellon University
essay_req_en: 3 required short answers (up to 300 words each): why you chose your major, how you define a successful college experience, and what you want to highlight. Prompts unchanged for the last two cycles.

name: University of Michigan--Ann Arbor
essay_req_en: 2 required U-M essays: how you are prepared to contribute to U-M's vision through leadership and citizenship (100-300 words) + why you chose the school/college you are applying to (100-550 words); 1 optional challenges essay. Same for 2026-27.
essay_change_en: In the 2025-26 cycle, dropped the long-standing 'community and your place within it' essay and replaced it with a leadership/citizenship (contributing to the vision) prompt (2-required-essay structure kept).

name: University of Notre Dame
essay_req_en: 1 required essay (150 words, your non-negotiable factor in choosing a college) + choose 2 of 4 short answers (50-100 words each: faith, personal experience, service, etc.).
essay_change_en: In the 2026-27 cycle, reduced the number of responses from 5 (2 required essays + 3 of 5 short answers) to 3 (1 required essay + 2 of 4 short answers).
merit_note_en: Stamps Scholars Program (full tuition and fees plus $12,000 enrichment fund; all REA/RD applicants automatically considered); other limited merit awards via Notre Dame Scholars' Program

name: Washington University in St. Louis
essay_req_en: 1 required essay (250 words, what you want to study and why) + optional 90-second video introduction. Optional writing supplements no longer offered.
essay_change_en: In the 2026-27 cycle, dropped all optional essay prompts (community / By Name & Story, etc.), keeping only 1 required major-interest essay (250 words) and the optional video.
merit_note_en: Signature Scholar Programs: Danforth Scholars, John B. Ervin Scholars, Annika Rodriguez Scholars (full- and partial-tuition)

name: Emory University
essay_req_en: 2 short answers: academic interest and why (200 words) + choose 1 of 4 options (150 words). 2026-27 prompts released as the same set as the previous cycle.
merit_note_en: Emory University Scholar Programs: Woodruff Scholars, Goizueta Scholars (merit, incoming first-years)

name: Georgetown University
essay_req_en: 4 required essays: the activity you have been most engaged in 250 words + an experience with someone of a different perspective 250 words (new) + personal/creative essay 650 words + school-specific essay 500 words. Submit via the Common App or Georgetown's own application.
essay_change_en: Starting with the 2026-27 cycle (Fall 2027 entry), adopted the Common App for the first time and overhauled the supplement — new 250-word 'encounter with a different perspective' essay, previous talents prompt dropped, and word limits specified instead of 'one page'.

name: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
essay_req_en: No supplemental essays. Only the Common App personal essay (250-650 words) is required.
essay_change_en: In the 2026-27 cycle, fully dropped the 2 previously required short answers (250 words each) — supplemental essays eliminated to simplify the application process (official announcement).
merit_note_en: Morehead-Cain, Robertson, Pogue, Carolina, Colonel Robinson, Johnston, Morrison, Blue Sky, Wood Family, Innovation, B. Robert Williamson Jr. (UNC Academic Scholarships)

name: University of Virginia
essay_req_en: 2026-27: No UVA-specific supplemental essay for general applicants — submit only the Common App personal essay. Only School of Nursing applicants are reportedly required to write 1 essay (250 words) on nursing-related experience (not listed on the official page).
essay_change_en: Starting with the 2025-26 cycle, the previously required short-answer prompts (e.g., the ~100-word 'personality/background' question) were fully removed, eliminating the supplement; the no-supplement approach continues in 2026-27 (nursing school is the only exception).

name: University of Southern California
merit_note_en: Trustee (full tuition), Presidential (half tuition), Deans (quarter tuition) - automatic consideration with Nov 1/Dec 1 application; ~15% of 2025 entering first-years received a USC merit scholarship

name: University of California, San Diego
essay_req_en: UC application Personal Insight Questions: choose 4 of 8, 350 words max each. No campus-specific essays. Same for both 2025-26 and 2026-27.
merit_note_en: Regents Scholarship for Entering Freshmen ($20,000 honorarium over 4 years; US citizens/PR/CA Dream Act only), Chancellor's Scholarship for Entering First-Year - automatic consideration from UC application

name: University of Florida
essay_req_en: No UF-specific supplemental essay. Common App personal essay required. Optional additional essays only for Honors Program and Innovation Academy applicants.
merit_note_en: Presidential Scholarship ($5,000/yr, in-state), Presidential Gold ($8,000), Presidential Platinum ($10,000), Stamps Scholars, Benacquisto (National Merit), Out-of-State Tuition Scholarships (Alumni/Sunshine/Gator Nation/Distinguished Scholar)

name: University of Texas at Austin
essay_req_en: 1 essay (open topic, 500-650 words — satisfied by the Common App personal essay) + 2 required short answers (interest in your first-choice major / the activity you are most proud of, 250-300 words each) + 1 optional short answer (circumstances that affected your academics).
merit_note_en: Texas Advance Commitment (in-state, AGI <= $125k, guaranteed need-based aid); first-year scholarships via LASSO Scholarship Finder (apply by Dec 1); Forty Acres Scholars (Texas Exes) referenced on admissions page

name: Georgia Institute of Technology
essay_req_en: 2026-27: Supplemental essay fully eliminated — submit only the Common App personal essay (choose 1 of 7 prompts). The only essay Georgia Tech reads.
essay_change_en: Officially announced July 29, 2026: starting with the 2026-27 cycle (Fall 2027 entry), the 'Why this major at Georgia Tech?' short-answer supplement is dropped — judged not to be a meaningful differentiator in admission decisions.
merit_note_en: Stamps President's Scholars (full ride, ~50/yr, automatic consideration via Early Action), Gold Scholars (partial, ~10-20/yr, top 2%); HOPE/Zell Miller for Georgia residents

name: New York University
essay_req_en: 1 optional supplemental essay — 'bridge builders' prompt (an experience bridging divides), 250 words or fewer. Same optional prompt kept for both 2025-26 and 2026-27.

name: University of California, Davis
essay_req_en: UC application Personal Insight Questions: choose 4 of 8, 350 words max each. No campus-specific essays. No change in the last two cycles.
merit_note_en: Regents Scholarship ($7,500/yr, first-year & third-year, via UC application); UC Davis campus-based scholarships (automatic consideration, min 3.25 GPA)

name: University of California, Irvine
essay_req_en: UC application Personal Insight Questions: choose 4 of 8, 350 words max each. No campus-specific essays. No change in the last two cycles.
merit_note_en: Regents' Scholarship (requires U.S. citizen, eligible non-citizen, or AB130/AB131 student; must be confirmed California resident to retain)

name: Boston College
essay_req_en: 1 writing supplement (400 words) — choose 1 of 4 prompts; Human-Centered Engineering majors answer a dedicated prompt. Number and required structure same as 2025-26.
merit_note_en: Presidential Scholarship (Gabelli Presidential Scholars Program) — BC's only academic merit scholarship, full tuition, 18 per year

name: Tufts University
essay_req_en: 2 required short responses — ① how you explored and engaged with Tufts (75-150 words), ② a school-specific prompt (A&S: a favorite assignment from the last 2 years / Engineering: an engineering or science project you took part in / BFA: a portfolio piece; 100-200 words each). Explicitly strongly discourages AI use.
essay_change_en: In 2026-27, 'Why Tufts' (50-100 words) was reworked into a 75-150-word prompt about how you explored the school, and the second essay changed from 'choose 1 of 3 (200-250 words)' to a single school-specific prompt (100-200 words).

name: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
essay_req_en: 2-3 required essays related to your major choice (first-choice major experience and career goals, ~150 words each; +1 if you choose a second-choice major) + Common App essay (250-650 words). Same format for years.
merit_note_en: University Scholarships (merit, automatic consideration for first-year and transfer applicants, any college)

name: University of Wisconsin--Madison
essay_req_en: Required essay: 'Why UW-Madison + interest in your chosen major' (650 words max, 300-500 recommended) — common to all applicants. Plus 1 Common App essay or Universities of Wisconsin application essay. No structural change.
merit_note_en: Scholarships via Wisconsin Scholarship Hub (WiSH) — incoming students automatically considered; no named university-wide first-year merit program on pages checked

name: University of California, Santa Barbara
essay_req_en: UC application Personal Insight Questions: choose 4 of 8, 350 words max each. No campus-specific essays. No change in the last two cycles.
merit_note_en: Regents Scholarship (all admitted fall freshmen considered via UC application; requires U.S. citizen, permanent resident, or AB130/AB131 student)

name: Ohio State University
essay_req_en: No school-specific supplemental essay. Only the Common App personal essay (choose one prompt, 250~650 words) is required. Additional essays only when applying separately to certain scholarship programs (e.g., Morrill).
merit_note_en: Stamps Eminence Scholarship, Morrill Scholarship Program, President's Ohio Scholarship, Land Grant Opportunity Scholarship, National Buckeye Scholarship, Maximus Scholarship, Provost Scholarship, Trustees Scholarship

name: Boston University
essay_req_en: 1 required supplement (up to 300 words): the single prompt "What about being a student at BU most excites you?" (no choice of prompts). Common App personal essay required separately.
essay_change_en: In 2025-26 it was a choice of 1 of 2 prompts (reflecting on a social/community issue / what excites you about BU + contribution) (300 words); starting in 2026-27 they were merged into a single prompt and the 'contribution' part was removed.
merit_note_en: Trustee Scholarship, Presidential Scholarship

name: Rutgers University--New Brunswick
essay_req_en: 1 essay required (Common App personal essay, 650 words, or Rutgers' own application, 3,800 characters). No Rutgers-specific supplemental essay. A short statement if interested in the Honors College; Mason Gross arts majors submit a separate audition/portfolio application.
merit_note_en: Automatic-consideration merit scholarships, National Merit College-Sponsored Merit Award

name: University of Maryland, College Park
essay_req_en: 1 main essay required (choose 1 of 7 prompts, 650 words max) + 6 required 'sentence-completion' short answers within the application (650 characters each incl. spaces, ~100 words). The 6 short answers are unchanged from 2025-26 (the official essay page lists only the main essay; the short answers appear within the application).
merit_note_en: Banneker/Key Scholarship, President's Scholarship, Dean's Scholarship

name: University of Washington (Seattle)
essay_req_en: Apply via the Common App; only the Common App personal essay (250~650 words) is required. No UW-specific required short responses. Optional: Common App 'Challenges and Circumstances' (250 words), 'Additional Information' (300 words).
essay_change_en: Through the previous cycle, the format was a UW-specified prompt essay (650 words) + a required community/diversity short response (300 words); per the official 2026-27 guidance, only the standard Common App essay is required and the UW-specific required short response was dropped.
merit_note_en: Purple & Gold Scholarship (nonresident US students), Presidential Scholarship (WA residents)

name: Lehigh University
merit_note_en: Dean's Scholarship, Founder's Scholarship, Trustees' Scholarship, Soaring Together Scholarship

name: Northeastern University
essay_req_en: No supplemental essay. Only the Common App/Coalition personal essay is required. Exception: Arts, Media and Design (CAMD) programs — a 500-word statement is included when submitting a portfolio (recommended).
merit_note_en: National Merit Finalist award, National Recognition Program Scholarship, Torch Scholars Program, Stamps Scholarship, Boston Scholarships

name: Purdue University--Main Campus
essay_req_en: Common App personal essay + 2 required Purdue-specific short answers (up to 250 words each): ① how Purdue's opportunities will support your interests in and out of the classroom ② why you chose your major and campus (West Lafayette/Indianapolis). 1 additional, identical question if you list an alternate major. Additional essays (200 words each) for Honors College applicants.
essay_change_en: Change within the last two cycles: the word limit for the 2 required short answers was raised from 100 to 250 words each (applied from 2025-26, unchanged for 2026-27).
merit_note_en: Trustees Scholarship, Presidential Scholarship, Indy Scholars, Lilly Scholars at Purdue, National Recognition Programs Scholarship

name: University of Georgia
essay_req_en: No UGA-specific supplemental essay. Only 1 Common App personal essay (250~650 words) is required.
essay_change_en: The UGA-specific short essay (200~300 words) required through Fall 2026 (2025-26 cycle) is dropped starting Fall 2027 (2026-27 cycle) — the official admissions blog states that one personal essay is enough.
merit_note_en: Foundation Fellowship; Presidential Leadership Scholarship; Classic Scholarship; Charter Scholarship; Dr. Henry King Stanford Scholarship; Woodruff / Baldwin / Harris / Charles McDonald Brown / Georgia Incentive (in-state only)

name: University of Rochester
essay_req_en: 1 required supplement (250 words max): a single prompt asking how you would combine academic flexibility and extracurricular opportunities at Rochester, where curiosity and creativity meet. Structure (1 required, 250 words) same as the previous cycle; only the prompt wording changed. Additional short answers if you indicate interest in Combined Degree programs or research. Explicitly discourages AI-written responses.
merit_note_en: Meliora Scholarship; Alan and Jane Handler Scholarship; Bausch + Lomb Honorary Science Award; Xerox Award; George Eastman Young Leaders Award; Frederick Douglass and Susan B. Anthony Award

name: Case Western Reserve University
essay_req_en: No supplemental essay for general applicants — only the Common App personal essay is required. Exceptions: 2 additional essays for the Pre-Professional Scholars Program (medicine/dentistry); Arts Supplement for music majors.
merit_note_en: University Scholarship; Bolton Scholarship; Michelson-Morley STEM Scholarship; scholarship competitions (Squire, A.W. Smith Innovation, FIRST, Wolf, etc.)

name: Florida State University
essay_req_en: No supplemental essay. 1 essay required (Common App personal essay prompts, 650 words max) — can be uploaded to the Admissions Portal after submitting the application.
merit_note_en: Presidential Scholars; Stamps Scholars; Vires Scholarship; Mores Scholarship; National Merit Finalist/Benacquisto; University Out-of-State Tuition Waiver; IB Diploma Scholarship; Sunshine Award

name: Texas A&M University
essay_req_en: Apply via ApplyTexas or the Common App. 1 required essay — Topic A "Tell us your story..." (opportunities/challenges that shaped you in high school). Plus several required short answers within the application (experiences that prepared you for success in college, why A&M, educational plans after your undergraduate degree, other experiences that affected your academic record, etc.). Length limits vary by platform (ApplyTexas uses character limits).
merit_note_en: President's Endowed Scholarship; Lechner Scholarship; McFadden Scholarship; President's Achievement Scholarship; Regents' Scholars Program; Maroon Merit Award; Century Scholars

name: Virginia Tech
essay_req_en: Common App personal essay not required. Instead, 4 Ut Prosim Profile short answers required of all applicants (120 words each): community contribution, experiences of inclusion/exclusion, leadership/pride experiences, etc. Cannot be edited after submission. Official page is titled '2026-2027 Short Answer Questions' — the 4-question, 120-word format is the same as the previous cycle.
merit_note_en: Beyond Boundaries Scholars; Presidential Scholarship Initiative (PSI); VT Scholars

name: Wake Forest University
essay_req_en: Required: "Why Wake?" (100 words max, supplement section). For additional short answers, respond to at most 1 of 4 prompts (list of 5 books you found interesting / intellectual curiosity / response to a Maya Angelou quote / open-topic Top 10 list). 'Sharing your voice' in writing or video is fully optional (explicitly stated as not required).
essay_change_en: Starting in 2026-27, short-answer prompts changed from multiple responses to choosing 1 of 4, and Why Wake? (100 words) moved to the supplement questions section — change announced on the official admissions blog (2026.7).
merit_note_en: Nancy Susan Reynolds Scholarship; Guy T. Carswell Scholarship; Joseph G. Gordon Scholarship; Stamps Scholarship; Graylyn Scholarship; Leadership and Character Scholarship; Presidential Scholarship for Distinguished Achievement

name: William & Mary
essay_req_en: No required supplemental essay. Up to 2 of 6 optional short-answer prompts may be submitted (a community important to you, academic interests/career, family/background, what sparked your interest in W&M, a challenge you faced, a tour of your neighborhood, etc.; ~300 words each). The school strongly encourages submitting up to 2.
merit_note_en: 1693 Scholars Program; James Monroe Scholars Program; Provost Scholar Awards (out-of-state first-years); William & Mary Scholars Awards — all first-year applicants automatically considered (wm.edu/admission/financialaid/types/scholarships/merit/)

name: University of California, Merced
essay_req_en: Common App not used — single UC application system. Instead of essays, Personal Insight Questions: choose 4 of 8, 350 words max each. All 8 prompts and the structure same as the previous cycle (common to all UC campuses; no campus-specific essays).
merit_note_en: Global Access Program Scholarship (international/nonresident first-years, $25,000/yr for 4 yrs, GPA 3.25+, automatic consideration); UC Merced International Student Scholarship (continuing international undergrads, approx. $5,000-$10,000 for 2025-26, competitive)

name: Villanova University
essay_req_en: 1 required writing supplement: choose 1 of 5 prompts (an experience advocating for equity/justice / a life lesson you want to share / why Villanova is your 'new home' / being misjudged based on your identity / a moment when someone leaned on your strength), ~250 words. Must differ from your Common App/Coalition main essay. Official page specifies the 2026-2027 cycle and warns of penalties for unauthorized AI use.
merit_note_en: Presidential Scholarship (25/yr; tuition, housing, meal plan, fees, textbooks); St. Martin de Porres Scholarship (full tuition & general fees); Villanova National Merit Scholarship ($500-$2,000); Goizueta Foundation Scholars (US citizens/PR only); Maguire Foundation (Philadelphia-area partner schools)

name: George Washington University
essay_req_en: School-specific supplemental essay not required. 1 optional Writing Supplement may be submitted via the Common App — the official application steps state 'Submit a Writing Supplement (Optional on Common App)'; no penalty for not submitting (word count not listed on the official page). Common App personal essay is submitted.
merit_note_en: Presidential Academic Scholarship (automatic consideration); You Are Welcome Here Scholarship (international, application required); Davis UWC Scholars partnership (need-based, up to full tuition & fees)

name: Pennsylvania State University--University Park
essay_req_en: No supplemental essay. The Personal Statement itself is optional — the official page states 'the optional Activities section and Personal Statement'. If you apply via the Common App, the Common App essay is accepted as the Penn State Personal Statement. (Only Schreyer Honors College applicants have separate essays.)
merit_note_en: Provost Academic Award (University Park; first-year non-PA residents; U.S. citizen or permanent resident only; amount varies by academic profile and need; automatic consideration)

name: Santa Clara University
essay_req_en: 1 optional supplemental essay, 150-300 words — prompt: how an SCU education will help you address an issue (local/global) that matters to you. Can be submitted anytime via the SCU application portal; not required.
essay_change_en: The required supplemental essay in 2025-26 was dropped; starting in 2026-27 it is reduced to 1 optional essay (150-300 words).
merit_note_en: Presidential at Entry Scholarship (full tuition); Provost Scholarship (half tuition); Dean's Scholarship (varies; international students eligible); Johnson Scholars Award (up to full tuition + room & board; international students not eligible) — first-year only, automatic review at admission

name: Stony Brook University (SUNY)
essay_req_en: No school-specific supplemental essay. An open-topic essay (Common App/SUNY App essay) is required. However, Honors College, WISE, and University Scholars require a ~250-word program-fit statement; Scholars for Medicine/Dental Medicine require an additional essay of 650 words or fewer; Creative Writing majors need a writing sample.
merit_note_en: Presidential Scholarships; Honors College Scholarships; Valedictorian and Salutatorian Scholarships; National Merit Scholarships; WISE; Regeneron STS Scholarships (automatic review of admitted first-years); Global Excellence Scholarship and #YouAreWelcomeHere (50% tuition) for international first-years

name: University of Minnesota, Twin Cities
essay_req_en: Essay not required — no supplemental essay. Per the official checklist, only the application, application fee, and self-reported academic record are required, and the Common App's official guidance also states 'No essays, letters of recommendation, ACT/SAT scores, or official transcripts are required to apply'. Short-response questions within the application are optional and used for review and scholarship consideration.
merit_note_en: Global Excellence Scholarship (international F-1 freshmen, $5,000-$20,000/yr for 4 yrs, automatic consideration, notified by end of March); U of M Gold Scholar Award (up to $10,000/yr, preference to National Merit Finalists naming UMN first choice); university-wide academic scholarships (automatic consideration, some need-based)

name: Williams College
essay_req_en: No required supplemental essay. Optionally, 1 academic writing sample (a school assignment, graded or ungraded) may be submitted — not an essay prompt.
merit_note_en: Official international financial aid page: "Although Williams isn't need-blind for international applicants, approximately 70% of international students receive financial aid from the college, with aid awards averaging more than $90,000 annually... Financial aid awards for international students are comprehensive, meet 100% of demonstrated need and are guaranteed for all four years." All-Grant program: "loans will never be included in your financial aid award from Williams." There are no merit scholarships (CDS H6: only need-based aid offered to nonresidents); all aid is need-based. International students must indicate their intent to apply for financial aid on the admission application.

name: Amherst College
essay_req_en: 1 required supplement: choose one of Option A (1 of 3 quotation prompts, up to 350 words) / Option B (submit a graded paper from grade 11-12) / Option C (A2A program applicants only).
merit_note_en: Official international student page: "Amherst College follows a need-blind admission policy for all students—domestic and international... Amherst meets 100% of calculated financial need for all international students who are admitted to the college and apply for need-based financial aid." The same page states "100% Calculated financial need met; no loans required", "82% International students with aid, 2025-2026", "$84,000+ Average international financial aid award, 2025–2026". Financial aid page: "we pride ourselves on being a no-loan school". There are no merit scholarships (CDS H6: only need-based aid offered to nonresidents); all aid is need-based.

name: Swarthmore College
essay_req_en: 2 required short answers (up to 250 words each): ① your identity/background and an experience collaborating across differences ② a topic that has fascinated you recently and your intellectual curiosity.
merit_note_en: Official international student page: "Admission to Swarthmore is need-aware for international citizens (excluding Permanent Residents, dual U.S. citizens, and DACA and undocumented students...)" / "if Swarthmore admits you and you applied for financial aid, the College meets 100% of your institutionally-determined financial need" / "Swarthmore is one of a small number of U.S. institutions that meets 100% of institutionally-determined financial need and does not include loans in the financial aid it offers to international students." No mention of merit scholarships (CDS H6: only need-based aid offered to nonresidents).

name: Bowdoin College
essay_req_en: No required supplemental essay. 2 optional essays (up to 250 words each): ① response to The Offer of the College ② Navigating through Differences. Separate optional video response.
merit_note_en: Official international student page: "Bowdoin College is need blind for international students. That means your family's ability to pay is not a factor or barrier to admission." / "Bowdoin is one of only eleven colleges and universities in the U.S. that are need-blind...and meets the full calculated need of every student we admit, including international students." / "$0 amount of loans in our financial aid packages." Financial aid page: "Our aid packages are loan free". No mention of merit scholarships (CDS H6: only need-based aid offered to nonresidents).

name: Claremont McKenna College
essay_req_en: 2 required supplemental essays: ① Why CMC (tied to the mission) ② Open Academy (an experience where a conversation with someone of a different perspective changed your attitudes/beliefs). Separate optional 2-minute video response.
merit_note_en: Official international student aid page: "CMC is need-aware in its admission process for all international students (non-U.S. citizens and non-U.S. permanent residents)... However, if admitted, CMC is committed to meeting demonstrated need as determined at the time of admission." / "Merit-based scholarships are available for all first-year applicants and are determined by the Office of Admission through the application review process." Apply by 12/1 for priority merit consideration. Scholarships page: McKenna Scholars ($15,000), Seaver Scholars (full-tuition). CDS H6: both need-based and non-need-based aid offered to nonresidents. Financial aid packages may include loans ("grants, scholarships, work, and loans").

name: Pomona College
essay_req_en: 2 required: Academic Interest Statement (150 words) + Short-Response Essay (choose 1 of 3 prompts, 250 words). As of 2026-08, the official page reflects Fall 2026 (not yet updated for 2026-27).
essay_change_en: In the 2025-26 cycle (Fall 2026), reduced from 3 essays (150+150+250 words) to 2 (150+250 words); 2026-27 prompts not yet published on the official page.
merit_note_en: Official: no academic or athletic scholarships (need-based only). Need-aware review for international students, but 100% of need is met for admitted students ("Admissions is need-aware for international applicants, but we meet the full need of every admitted international student"). Aid packages do not include loans ("Pomona does not use loans to meet a student's financial need").

name: Wellesley College
essay_req_en: 1 required Wellesley-specific essay: 'build bridges' prompt (an experience working with people of different backgrounds/perspectives) — separate from the Common App personal essay (250-650 words).
merit_note_en: Official: no merit scholarships, academic, athletic, or otherwise ("We do not offer academic, athletic or other scholarships"). Not need-blind for international students (non-citizens/non-permanent residents) ("Wellesley is not need-blind for students who are not U.S. citizens or permanent residents"); a limited number of need-based awards; 100% of calculated need met for admitted students ("committed to meeting 100% of calculated need for all admitted international citizens who have applied for financial aid during the admission process").

name: Carleton College
essay_req_en: No supplemental essay (Common App main essay only). The Carleton Supplement form includes only personal information, how-you-heard-about-us questions, and an optional free-response field; no essay prompts.
merit_note_en: Official: no merit scholarships ("We do not offer merit scholarships"; "All Carleton grants and scholarships are need-based"). Financial aid funding for international students is limited ("We have limited funding available to international students", "We offer a few need-based scholarships to international students"), and new aid applications are not accepted after admission. 100% of need met for all students ("we meet 100% of demonstrated need for every student"). Loans are included in small amounts ("We keep loans small and work-study manageable").

name: Harvey Mudd College
essay_req_en: 2 required additional writings: ① how your experiences/community shaped 'the problems you want to solve and the impact you want to make' (up to 500 words) ② an experience of asking for help to create change (up to 250 words).
essay_change_en: In 2026-27, both required prompts were fully replaced — the previous mission/background prompt (500 words) + 'dream HSA class' (100 words) became a new experience/impact prompt (500 words) + 'asking for help' essay (250 words), with the second prompt's length expanded from 100 to 250 words.
merit_note_en: Official: need-aware for international students ("Because funding for international students is limited, your level of financial need may affect your chances for admission if you apply for financial aid"). Meeting 100% of need is possible for only a very small number of international students ("We are able to meet 100% of a family's demonstrated need for only a handful of international students") → meets_full_need_intl false. International students may also be eligible for some merit awards, and the So Scholarship is exclusively for international students. CDS 2025-26 H6: both need-based and non-need-based checked as 'offered'. Loans are included in packages (CDS H1 student loans, Private alternative loans).

name: Barnard College
essay_req_en: 2 required short answers: ① 'bold question' (up to 50 words) ② a lesson you would learn from a woman whose perspective and problem-solving approach differ from yours but who excels at bringing people together (200-250 words).
essay_change_en: Reduced from 3 questions (200+150+150 words) to 1 question (200-250 words) in 2025-26, then reorganized into 2 required questions in 2026-27 with the addition of a 50-word 'bold question'.
merit_note_en: Official: no merit scholarships ("Barnard gives no merit scholarships"). Need-aware for international students (non-citizens/non-permanent residents) ("We are need-aware for non-U.S. citizens and non-permanent residents"), with only a small number of need-based awards per entering class. 100% of need met for admitted students ("Barnard will meet 100% of the financial need of admitted students"). Aid packages combine grants, loans, and jobs (loans included).

name: Davidson College
essay_req_en: Personal essay (250-650 words) + 2 required supplemental essays — ① Why Davidson (250-300 words) ② a topic/activity/idea that interests you (250-300 words).
merit_note_en: Official: 'First-year applicants, including both domestic and international students, can be considered for Davidson's non-need-based scholarships.' Financial aid packages do not include loans (The Davidson Trust).

name: Grinnell College
essay_req_en: No required supplement — Common App essay only ('no required supplement' officially stated). If you wish, additional materials (writing samples, essays, etc.) can be attached via the portal after submitting.
merit_note_en: International students' need is met through 'a combination of grants and student employment' (no loans). Official: 'Grinnell College has a need-aware admission policy for international students'.

name: Hamilton College
essay_req_en: No required supplement — 1 optional supplemental short answer (can be completed on any platform or in the applicant portal after submitting) + optional materials such as a Hamilton Hello video or a personal URL.
merit_note_en: No merit scholarships (official FAQ: 'Hamilton discontinued offering merit scholarships with the class that entered in the Fall of 2008'). Need-based packages include small loans (up to $3,500 in the first year).

name: Middlebury College
essay_req_en: No supplement — officially states that no supplemental essay is required; submit only the Common App/Coalition personal essay (art portfolio optional, via SlideRoom).
merit_note_en: No merit scholarships (official: 'All of Middlebury's financial aid is need based. We don't offer merit aid'). International students' need is met with 'a combination of work, loans, and grants'.

name: Smith College
essay_req_en: No supplement — submit only 1 Common App/Coalition essay (school-specific supplemental questions remain eliminated; arts supplement optional).
merit_note_en: Official: 'Smith has eliminated loans from its undergraduate financial aid packages for those students receiving institutional need-based aid, replacing those funds with institutional grants.' International students must apply for financial aid by the deadline before admission (if they do not, they are permanently ineligible afterward).

name: Vassar College
merit_note_en: Financial aid is entirely need-based ("Financial aid is awarded exclusively on the basis of need") and there are no merit scholarships. International students must apply for financial aid at the same time as applying for admission, and the admissions office is need-aware when reviewing international students.

name: Wesleyan University
essay_req_en: No supplement — Common App/Coalition personal essay only; no school-specific additional essays (only optional portfolio/supplementary materials may be submitted).
merit_note_en: "We do not include loans in our undergraduate financial aid packages." International students must apply for financial aid at the time they apply for admission (if they do not, they are ineligible for aid for all four years), and aid applicants who are citizens of 11 Asian countries, including Korea, are considered for the Freeman Asian Scholarship Program (4-year full scholarship). However, it explicitly states "admission for international students seeking financial aid is extremely competitive".

name: Washington and Lee University
essay_req_en: No required supplement — optional short-answer statement (respond to a short essay prompt in the applicant portal in writing or with a 2-minute video). 1 essay of up to 800 words required only for Johnson Scholarship applicants (deadline 2026-12-01).
merit_note_en: "W&L admits students without considering their ability to pay" — need-blind for domestic, international, and undocumented students alike. "W&L meets the full demonstrated financial need of every admitted applicant entirely through grants and student employment, without loans." Merit aid is consolidated into the Johnson Scholarship (up to 44 students; full tuition + room + board), which international students may also apply for. W&L Promise: households with income under $200,000 receive at least a full-tuition grant. However, the international student page includes the statement "Admission to Washington and Lee does not guarantee financial assistance".

name: Colgate University
essay_req_en: No required supplement — optional supplemental prompts (up to 250 words each, e.g., what you gain from engaging with a diverse community / what inspires you). Officially states there is no penalty for not submitting.
merit_note_en: "Colgate does not offer academic merit scholarships" — entirely need-based. International student page: "We consider financial need during the review process for all applicants" (need-aware), "Colgate meets 100% of demonstrated financial need for every admitted student." The Colgate Commitment (for household income of $300,000 or less) is limited to U.S. citizens and permanent residents, and whether international students' packages include loans could not be confirmed on the official pages.

name: University of Richmond
essay_req_en: 1 required supplement — Richmond Question (choose 1 of the given prompts, 650 words max). The format (1 required, 650 words) stays the same; only the prompt wording is updated each year — 2026-27 prompts officially released.
merit_note_en: "The University of Richmond is committed to meeting the full demonstrated financial need of all admitted domestic and international applicants." International students are reviewed need-aware ("the Office of Admission is need-aware when reviewing applications from non-U.S. citizens and non-U.S. permanent residents"), and "International students... may receive full consideration for all merit-based scholarships, with the exception of the Army ROTC scholarship program" — Richmond Scholars consideration is automatic when applying by 12/1. International students must submit a Certification of Financial Responsibility.

name: Bates College
essay_req_en: No supplement — Common App personal essay only; no additional essay item on the official checklist (arts/creative supplement optional; supplement eliminated since the 2017-18 cycle).
merit_note_en: Bates officially states that its financial aid is entirely need-based and that it does not offer merit scholarships to international students. It officially states that it meets 100% of calculated need for non-U.S.-citizen applicants without loans (grant + on-campus work), and that it is not need-blind (need-aware).

name: Colby College
essay_req_en: No supplemental essay — no additional writing required beyond the Common App/Coalition/QuestBridge personal essay. Only optional materials such as the Arts Supplement and InitialView may be submitted.
merit_note_en: Colby Commitment: officially states that it meets 100% of calculated need for all admitted students (including international students) without loans (grant + on-campus work). No merit scholarships (academic, athletic, or other talent-based) (only a $2,000 National Merit Finalist recognition award). The admissions FAQ officially states 'Colby is need aware'.

name: Haverford College
essay_req_en: 2 required supplements — ① a topic that sparks your intellectual curiosity and how you would explore it at Haverford (150-200 words) ② the community values represented by the Honor Code and the values you are looking for (150-200 words).
merit_note_en: All financial aid is need-based (no merit). Officially states that it provides financial aid to a limited number of international students each year and that students who receive aid have their full calculated need met. International students who do not receive aid in their first year cannot receive it in later years either.

name: College of the Holy Cross
essay_req_en: No school-specific supplemental essay — the official application checklist (application, transcript, 2 recommendations, application fee) has no additional essay item. Only supplementary materials such as evidence of special talents may be optionally submitted.
merit_note_en: The financial aid page officially states that it meets 100% of calculated need for all admitted international students, while the international student page states that funding for international students is limited (limited funding). There are a few merit scholarships, but international eligibility is not specified. Packages include federal and institutional loans (not no-loan). Households with income of $100,000 or less (with typical assets) receive a full-tuition grant.

name: Macalester College
essay_req_en: 2 optional essays — in the Common App member section: ① how the Twin Cities location benefits your academic/social/community experience ② how you connect with the 4 core values (academic excellence, internationalism, multiculturalism, service to society). Neither is required.
merit_note_en: The international student FAQ officially states that financial need plays a role in admission decisions (need-aware), and also that it meets the full calculated need of every enrolling student. Merit for international students: Charles J. Turck Presidential Honor Scholarship ($15,000-35,000 per year, automatic consideration). Intent to apply for aid must be indicated at the time of application; aid cannot be requested after admission.

name: Mount Holyoke College
essay_req_en: 1 optional writing supplement — listed on the official application process page as 'Mount Holyoke writing supplement (optional)'. Common App/Coalition personal essay required separately.
merit_note_en: Official international student page: 45% of new international students receive need-based scholarships (average USD 58,686) or merit scholarships. International students' need-based packages consist of grants + fixed-rate student loans + on-campus work, and the loan portion is stated to increase by at least $1,000 each year.

name: Bryn Mawr College
essay_req_en: 1 required writing supplement (250-500 words, submitted via the Common App) — 'Bryn Mawr students bring their authentic selves to campus...' prompt. At the time of research, the official page was labeled 2025-26 (prompt unchanged since 2024-25).
merit_note_en: Official international student page: "International students are not eligible for merit aid." Need-based aid is available, but the page states "Bryn Mawr is a need-sensitive institution, meaning that while we meet the full calculated need of all admitted students, we have a limited amount of funds available". New financial aid applications not accepted after admission (must apply when applying for admission).

name: Bucknell University
essay_req_en: No long-form supplemental essay — only 1 school-specific question: a short answer (up to 250 words) explaining why you chose your first-choice major (or undecided) and second-choice major.
merit_note_en: Official international financial aid page: "Bucknell is currently not 'need-blind' for international students", "Bucknell financial aid for international students is limited", "only a small number of highly qualified international applicants are ultimately chosen to receive financial assistance". International students who do not receive aid in their first year receive none in later years. International eligibility is not specified for the merit programs (Presidential Fellowship $30,000, Dean's Scholarship $20,000, Engineering/Management/Malesardi Merit Scholars $40,000, etc.).

name: Colorado College
essay_req_en: 1 optional supplemental essay (300 words max) — Block Plan-style prompt on 'an experience of deeply immersing yourself in one thing'. The official page (marked 2026-27) states there is no penalty for not submitting.
merit_note_en: Official: "CC meets 100% of every student's demonstrated financial need" / "Colorado College meets the full demonstrated need for all students". International student page: "International applicants seeking financial aid comprise our most competitive group of applicants each year"; only a handful out of thousands can receive full aid. International students not applying for aid must demonstrate the ability to pay the full cost for 8 semesters. New financial aid applications not accepted after admission.

name: Lafayette College
essay_req_en: 1 optional 'Why Lafayette?' essay (20-200 words) — on the Common App member page; not required.
merit_note_en: Official: "Lafayette is proud to be one of only a select few colleges in the United States to guarantee to meet full demonstrated financial need of all admitted students, both domestic and international." However, "Lafayette College is need aware and considers a student's financial situation when making admission decisions." International students who do not receive aid in their first year cannot receive it later (budget constraints). Merit scholarships are decided by the admissions office without a separate application.

name: Denison University
essay_req_en: No supplemental essay — the official application page states 'No Supplemental Essay Required'. Submit only the Common App/Coalition personal essay.
merit_note_en: Official page: "International students are eligible for the same institutional need-based financial aid and merit-based scholarships as domestic students"; merit scholarships range from $5,000 per year to full tuition. However, "Denison is need-aware in the application process" (needing aid affects admission competitiveness).

name: Franklin & Marshall College
essay_req_en: No supplemental essay — no additional essay item on the official application checklist. Only supplemental materials such as a portfolio may be optionally submitted.
merit_note_en: International student page: "If you're admitted to F&M, we will meet 100% of your institutionally determined financial need for all four years" / "If you require a high level of aid, the admission process becomes more competitive" (need-aware). The financial aid page mentions 'Merit & Dedicated Scholarships (determined by the Office of Admission)', but individual names and international eligibility are not stated.

name: Occidental College
essay_req_en: 1 optional short answer (250 words max) — 'Why Occidental / why Oxy is the right place for you' prompt. The official checklist (Fall 2027 entry = 2026-27 cycle) states 'not mandatory'.
merit_note_en: International student page: "Need-based financial aid for international students is very limited and highly competitive" / "Occidental typically offers need-based aid to only a small number of international applicants". The cost & financial aid page states '100% demonstrated financial need met' (for all students overall). The official site mentions a minimum $15,000-per-year scholarship for ED admits.

name: Pitzer College
essay_req_en: 1 required writing supplement (650 words max) — choose 1 of 2 prompts (① your engagement with one of the 5 core values ② the college experience you want and your fit with Pitzer).
merit_note_en: Financial aid page: "We meet 100% of students' demonstrated need." Merit scholarships listed are the Trustee Community Scholarship ($5,000 per year, renewable) and Academic Achievement Scholarship ($2,000 one-time), but international eligibility is not stated. International students apply for need-based aid through the PIFAA (Pitzer International Financial Aid Application) (no CSS Profile/FAFSA submitted).

name: Scripps College
merit_note_en: International financial aid page: "A limited amount of financial aid is available to international students" / "Scripps College is need aware in our admission process" / financial aid is determined only at the time of admission. Main financial aid page: "Scripps meets 100 percent of a student's institutionally determined financial need." International eligibility for merit scholarships is not stated.

name: Indiana University Bloomington
essay_req_en: No separate supplemental essay — only 1 essay required. If applying via Apply IU, an IU-specific prompt (200-400 words, your academic/career plans and the activities you want to do at IU); if applying via the Common App, one of the Common App essay prompts may be used instead.
merit_note_en: International first-year applicants who apply by the Nov 1 early action deadline are automatically considered for IU academic scholarships (no separate application; amounts not published). Named international awards also exist (C.V. Starr, Rising Star, etc.) plus the one-time $7,500 Global Citizen Scholarship (separate video application).

name: Michigan State University
essay_req_en: No MSU-specific supplemental essay. 1 essay required (250-650 words) — choose from 7 prompts (including an open topic); this corresponds to the Common App personal essay. Used to improve admission chances and in scholarship review.
merit_note_en: MSU states that all international students admitted to MSU are automatically considered for its non-resident/international scholarships and that no application beyond the application for admission is required; published award levels are President's $15,000, Provost's $12,000, Dean's $10,000, 1855 Scholarship $7,000, Beaumont Tower $5,000 and Global Community Scholars $3,000 per year. Applying by the November 1 Early Action deadline is required for maximum scholarship consideration, and MSU notes that meeting the criteria does not guarantee an award.

name: North Carolina State University
essay_req_en: Common App/Coalition essay (650 words or fewer) required + 1 required NC State short answer — 'why you chose the major(s) selected above and why you want to study at NC State' (word count not listed on the official page; 250 words max per guidance). University Honors Program applicants add an essay of 600 words or fewer (optional, 11/1 deadline, same prompt as Park Scholarships).
essay_change_en: The second short answer asking why you chose your second-choice major was removed, leaving 1 short answer on why you chose your major.
merit_note_en: NC State states that international applicants are not eligible for financial aid, but that a limited number of competitive merit-based scholarships are available to international students. Admitted students access the PACK ASSIST scholarship portal and must submit the general scholarship application; the Park Scholarship is restricted to U.S. citizens, permanent residents, or graduates of a U.S. high school.

name: Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute
essay_req_en: No supplemental essay for general applicants — the general essay/personal statement in the application meets the essay requirement ('satisfies our requirements'). However, applicants to Architecture, Electronic Arts, Games and Simulation Arts and Sciences, Music, and Physician-Scientist (B.S./M.D.) must submit program-specific essays (Common App writing supplement).
merit_note_en: RPI states that it offers a limited number of merit-based scholarship opportunities for international undergraduate students, including awards of up to $20,000 per year, and that additional institutional funding may be available to recipients of the Rensselaer Medal Scholarship or Division I athletic scholarships. The Rensselaer Medal is awarded through partner high schools worldwide to students distinguished in mathematics and science and is worth $40,000 per year, guaranteed for four years (five for the B.Arch.). Apart from Canadian citizens, who may be considered for an institutional need-based grant, RPI advises international students to plan to cover the full cost of attendance.

name: University of Massachusetts Amherst
merit_note_en: UMass Amherst states that international undergraduate students are considered for merit scholarships by the Admissions Office as part of their admission to the university, and that first-year applicants are automatically considered with no separate application; awards are communicated in the acceptance letter and renew automatically with full-time enrollment and satisfactory academic progress. It also states that international students are not eligible for most types of financial aid because the FAFSA is limited to U.S. citizens and eligible non-citizens, and that additional scholarships may be available through a student's school, college or major.

name: University of Miami
essay_req_en: No supplemental essay — official announcement: 'The University of Miami does not require a supplemental essay for first-year admission as of the 2026-2027 application cycle.' Submit only the Common App personal essay (required). Some programs such as the Frost School of Music require separate application materials (auditions, etc.).
essay_change_en: Starting in 2026-27, Miami's own supplemental essay prompt was dropped; only the Common App personal essay is required.
merit_note_en: Miami states that all students who apply are automatically considered for its merit scholarships regardless of citizenship status and that no additional scholarship application is required, with the largest awards going to those who apply by the November 1 early deadlines; standard awards are the President's Scholarship (up to $30,000 per year) and the Canes Achievement Award (up to $20,000 per year). Its premier awards open to all incoming first-year students are the Stamps Scholarship (full cost of attendance plus a $12,000 enrichment fund) and the Isaac Bashevis Singer Scholarship (full tuition), while the Hammond and Weeks scholarships are limited to U.S. citizens and permanent residents.

name: Brandeis University
merit_note_en: "The Wien Scholarship is awarded to exceptional international applicants who demonstrate strong academic achievement and extracurricular or community involvement" and "meets the full demonstrated financial need of each recipient"; there is no separate application - all candidates offered admission are considered. Brandeis also administers the Davis United World College Scholars Program ($10,000 grant for UWC graduates with financial need) and the Toshizo Watanabe International Scholarship for students graduating from a Japanese high school.

name: Tulane University
essay_req_en: No supplemental essay — the items listed in the official Application Instructions are only the application (including activities list and personal statement), transcript, recommendations, and optional test scores; there is no additional essay such as 'Why Tulane'. The Common App personal essay (personal statement) is required.
essay_change_en: The optional 'Why Tulane' supplemental essay was discontinued (dropped) starting with the 2026-27 cycle; only the personal essay is submitted.
merit_note_en: "All applicants are considered for partial merit scholarship by completing the Common Application," and Tulane says its merit awards "may cover your full tuition and fees or may even cover your full cost of attendance"; "Tulane's Global Scholarships are renewable for 4 years (5 years for students in the 5-year Architecture program)." Separately, "Tulane offers up to $30,000 in need-based financial aid to international students," which requires the CSS Profile (recommended by February 15).

name: University of Connecticut
essay_req_en: No supplemental essay. Common App/Coalition personal essay required (recommended range 250-650 words) — officially stated as 'The personal essay is required'. Only nursing (DeLuca School of Nursing) applicants answer 1 additional question on their motivation for nursing.
merit_note_en: UConn lists the Global Excellence Award, Global Distinction Award and Global Leader Award as merit-based scholarships "available to international applicants; all campuses," renewable for four years at a fixed amount set yearly. First-year applicants are automatically considered for most merit scholarships on initial review, except the Nutmeg, Day of Pride and Stamps Scholarships, which require a supplemental application.

name: University of Pittsburgh
essay_req_en: No supplemental essay. An essay is not required for admission itself — the official required items are only the application, fee, STARS (self-reported grades), and optional test scores. However, a personal statement is needed to be considered for scholarships ('required to be considered for scholarships'), so submitting one is effectively recommended. Frederick Honors College is reviewed separately.
merit_note_en: "International first-year applicants who apply by February 1 are automatically considered for merit-based scholarships" of up to $10,000 per year, typically available for eight full-time undergraduate terms and renewable with Satisfactory Academic Progress; no separate application is required, but the international short answer, Common Application essay or a personal statement must be submitted and awards apply only to fall (August) entry.

name: Binghamton University (SUNY)
essay_req_en: No supplement. No school-specific supplemental essay required beyond the main essay in the Common App/SUNY App/Coalition application (no essay item on the official checklist).

name: Clemson University
essay_req_en: No supplement. An essay is not an admission requirement at all; all additional materials such as a personal statement are optional ('Clemson does not require any of these additional materials for admission').

name: Rutgers University--Newark
essay_req_en: No supplement. 1 main essay required — Rutgers' own application: 3,800 characters (incl. spaces); Common App: up to 650 words. Officially states there is no supplemental essay for the Common App route; a short statement is added only when applying for Honors.

name: Syracuse University
essay_req_en: No supplement. No writing supplement item on the official checklist (Common App main essay only). However, Architecture and Visual and Performing Arts require additional college-specific materials such as a portfolio/audition.
merit_note_en: Syracuse's financial aid office states, "All students who apply for admission to Syracuse University are considered for merit-based scholarships, regardless of citizenship or country of birth," and that international undergraduates are considered for merit scholarships based on their application for admission. No separate scholarship application is required.

name: University at Buffalo (SUNY)
essay_req_en: No supplement. No school-specific supplemental essay required beyond the Common App/Coalition main essay (official requirements: transcript and major selection; recommendations and test scores optional).
merit_note_en: UB states it "offers scholarships in varying amounts to qualified incoming international first-year/first-time students" and that "All admitted international students are automatically considered for scholarships during the holistic review process," renewable for up to four years if continuing eligibility requirements are met. UB advises applying by November 1 for priority scholarship consideration.

name: University of California, Riverside
essay_req_en: UC common application Personal Insight Questions: respond to 4 of 8, up to 350 words each. No campus-specific additional essays.
merit_note_en: UCR states that first-year nonresident students "may receive up to $89,100 for four years" and that international students are automatically considered upon acceptance once confirmed as nonresidents and meeting UC eligibility requirements, with a 3.0 GPA required to keep the award while at UCR. No separate scholarship application is required.

name: Colorado School of Mines
essay_req_en: No supplement. The essay is an optional, not required, submission (considered only as optional material in holistic review).
merit_note_en: Mines states that "International First-Year Students are eligible for up to $8,000 in an admissions award"; the application is evaluated for merit aid by the Undergraduate Admissions Office and the award is renewable for 8 consecutive semesters toward tuition and fees. Students with an outside sponsorship may not be eligible, and the Financial Aid Office states that international students are generally not eligible for (need-based) financial aid.

name: Drexel University
essay_req_en: No supplement. 1 Common App/Coalition (Scoir) main essay of 250–650 words required; no Drexel-specific supplemental essay.
merit_note_en: Drexel states that "Students admitted through Early Decision are eligible for a minimum of $20,000 in merit scholarships along with consideration for need-based aid," and its international admissions page states that "Drexel does offer need-based aid to qualifying international students." Merit awards are made by the Admissions Committee on the basis of academic performance with no separate application; per CDS H6, 1,038 nonresident undergraduates received institutional aid averaging $32,937 in 2024-2025.

name: New Jersey Institute of Technology
essay_req_en: No supplement. Only the Common App main essay is used in evaluation; no NJIT-specific supplemental essay required.
merit_note_en: NJIT states that "Although international students aren't eligible for federal aid, there are plenty of other opportunities for financial assistance," and points international students to NJIT scholarships. Merit awards require no separate application: "Once you are admitted as a first-time, full-time freshman, your academic records such as SAT/ACT scores and high school GPA, are reviewed to determine your eligibility for NJIT scholarships," and most require full-time enrollment and a 3.0 GPA to renew. No international-specific award name or dollar amount is published officially.

name: Stevens Institute of Technology
essay_req_en: No supplement. 1 main essay included in the application ('Essay — included on your application') required; no Stevens-specific supplemental essay. Portfolio strongly recommended for Music and Visual Arts & Technology applicants.
merit_note_en: Stevens states that "Stevens awards a limited number of merit scholarships to international students" and that it "may offer a merit based Global Scholarship to international students with exceptional academic achievement." International students who want to be considered for institutional scholarships must file the CSS Profile (school code 2819); no dollar amounts are published.

name: Pepperdine University
essay_req_en: 1 required supplement: why you are applying to Pepperdine, a Christian university, and how you would contribute to faith conversations on campus (300–500 words). Submitted in addition to the Common App main essay.
merit_note_en: All admitted students are automatically considered for the Blanche E. Seaver International Scholars' Awards; no separate application is required, and the merit-based award is offered to a limited number of candidates. Recipients must maintain a 3.25 Pepperdine cumulative GPA and full-time status; Pepperdine also names the Charles Lam Scholarship ($8,000-$10,000/yr, citizens of Mainland China) and the Lydia Hayne Scholarship Fund (full tuition, room and board, citizens of an African country, offered once every four years).

name: University of Illinois Chicago
essay_req_en: Common App main essay required + 1 required short essay in the UIC Member Profile (on your intended major or career field of interest). Word count not listed on the official page.

name: Worcester Polytechnic Institute
essay_req_en: No supplement. The official application requirements (Common App, transcript, recommendations) include no WPI-specific supplemental essay.
merit_note_en: WPI offers competitive academic merit-based scholarships to first-year and transfer applicants based on academic performance, leadership experiences, extracurricular involvement, and community service; all applicants for admission are automatically considered and no additional application is required. IB diploma graduates with a diploma score of 40 or greater admitted as first-year students are guaranteed a merit scholarship worth a minimum of $25,000, and starting with students entering in fall 2026 all students admitted under an Early Decision plan are offered a minimum merit scholarship of $25,000 per year for up to four years.

name: Yeshiva University
essay_req_en: Per YU's own application: 1 main essay (choose from 7 prompts) + 1 Personal Statement required (how YU will support your academic goals and help you grow personally and in your values, 250 words max). Interview required for all applicants. The official page lists prompts for 'Spring 2027 admissions and beyond'.
merit_note_en: Yeshiva University's international admissions page states that YU offers merit-based scholarships to international students, and that although U.S. federal and state financial aid is not available to non-citizens, students may also be considered for institutional need-based aid; an international aid application is added to the applicant portal after applying. No named international merit program is published on the official admissions pages.

name: American University
essay_req_en: 1 optional supplement: 'American University students identify as changemakers... Describe a belief, hobby, idea, issue, or topic about which you're excited' (2026-2027 cycle specified; word count not listed on the checklist page). Main essay required.
merit_note_en: AU states that qualified international first-year applicants are automatically considered, with no separate application, for partial merit scholarships of $8,000 to $25,000 per year, renewable for four years. The separately-applied AU Emerging Global Leader Scholarship covers all billable expenses for two students, with up to eight additional partial awards of up to $40,000 per year. AU states that no need-based financial aid is available to international students.

name: Baylor University
essay_req_en: 1 main essay required (goBAYLOR or Common App). The Short Answer Response ('Why Baylor / contribution', ~450 words) is required only for 11/1 Early Decision (binding) applicants; recommended (optional) for all other applicants.
merit_note_en: Admitted first-time international students are automatically considered for merit-based scholarships based on a complete review of their high school academic performance. For need-based consideration Baylor requires the CSS Profile (code 6032) by the November 1 priority deadline or the February 1 regular deadline; beginning with Fall 2027 a new Baylor International Financial Aid Application (BIFAA) opens October 1 with a November 1 priority and February 1 final deadline.

name: Howard University
essay_req_en: Common App main essay required + 1 optional essay (accessed in the Common App Writing section; no obligation to submit).
merit_note_en: Howard states that international applicants must submit the HU ISFAA to be considered for financial aid, and that applicants who do not submit test scores receive equal consideration for scholarships based on other academic achievements. Applying by the deadline of the chosen admission plan is required for priority scholarship consideration. No international-specific named merit program is published on the admission site.

name: Marquette University
essay_req_en: No supplement. 1 main essay (personal statement) required (Common App or Marquette's own application). Additional personal statements and recommendations not required (reviewed only if submitted).
merit_note_en: All admitted international undergraduates are automatically considered for Marquette merit scholarships, including the Père Marquette Award, at the time of admission; some additional merit scholarships require a separate application after admission. Marquette states that it is not able to award need-based scholarships to international students.

name: Rochester Institute of Technology
essay_req_en: No supplement. 1 Common App/RIT application main essay required. 1 additional supplemental essay required only for Honors Program or Individualized Program BS applicants.
merit_note_en: RIT states that first-year merit scholarships range from $14,000 to $30,000 annually ($56,000 to $120,000 over the degree) and that all applicants, including international applicants, are considered for merit scholarships just by applying, with awards announced at the time of admission. RIT states that full-cost or full-tuition scholarships are not typically offered to undergraduates and that only very limited need-based funding is available; total support must reach at least $78,000 USD for RIT to issue the I-20.

name: Southern Methodist University
essay_req_en: No required supplement. Main essay of 250–650 words required on the application platform (Common App, ApplyTexas, SMU's own application, Coalition); the official requirements page lists no SMU-specific required supplemental essay.
merit_note_en: All students who apply to SMU, regardless of citizenship, are automatically considered for SMU's academic merit scholarships with no separate application. Automatic consideration requires applying by November 1 (Early Decision I / Early Action) or January 15 (Early Decision II / Regular Decision); need-based financial aid is available only to U.S. citizens and permanent residents.

name: University of California, Santa Cruz
essay_req_en: UC common application Personal Insight Questions: respond to 4 of 8, up to 350 words each. No campus-specific additional essays.
merit_note_en: Newly admitted out-of-state and international first-year students are automatically considered for the Undergraduate Dean's Award during the admissions cycle; first-year awards range from $12,000 to $100,000 paid evenly over four years ($3,000-$25,000 per year). International students are not eligible for federal, state, or university need-based aid.

name: University of Delaware
essay_req_en: No supplement — submit only the Common App/Coalition personal essay (required); no additional essays.
merit_note_en: All first-year international applicants are automatically considered for UD merit scholarships of $5,000-$15,000 per year, with no separate scholarship application. International students may also compete for UD's Distinguished Scholars awards, which can cover tuition plus room and board for four years if a 3.0 GPA is maintained.

name: University of South Florida
essay_req_en: No essay — only the application (USF's own or Common App) + fee + SSAR self-reported grades + test scores required; no personal essay or supplement (separate application only for Judy Genshaft Honors College).
merit_note_en: Admitted international students are automatically considered, with no separate application, for the Green and Gold Presidential (about $44,000 total, up to $11,000 per year), Directors (about $36,000, up to $9,000 per year), and Scholars (about $20,000, up to $5,000 per year) waiver awards. These are partial out-of-state tuition waivers, require completing the freshman application by the January 15 scholarship deadline, and cannot be combined with another tuition-waiver scholarship.

name: Florida International University
essay_req_en: No essay — only the Common App application, test scores (SAT/ACT/CLT), and transcript required; no personal essay or supplement (personal statement only for Honors College applicants).
merit_note_en: FIU states it automatically considers admitted first-time-in-college students for merit-based scholarships when they submit and complete the freshman admissions application by the posted date (December 3, 2025 for students attending out-of-state or overseas high schools for Early Fall/Fall 2026), including official SAT, ACT or CLT scores. Eligible students must be U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents, or international students receiving an F-1 (or another eligible) visa; no additional application is required.

name: Fordham University
essay_req_en: No required supplement — Common App essay (required) + 3 optional short responses (Unique Fordham question, Additional information, Challenges and circumstances). Listed as 'Optional application components' on the official page, as of the 2026-27 deadlines.
merit_note_en: Fordham states that all complete applications for admission are automatically considered for merit scholarships, that no supplementary materials are required, and that merit award notifications are included within the online admission letter. Its International Student Scholarships page lists competitive four-year awards, including the full-tuition Presidential Scholarship for entering first-year students who generally rank in the top 1-2 percent of their high school class.

name: Rutgers University--Camden
essay_req_en: No supplement — Rutgers' own application requires 1 essay (up to 3,800 characters; choose 1 of 7 prompts or an open topic); the Common App requires only the personal essay (250-650 words). Officially states there is no supplemental essay when applying via the Common App (only a short statement added if being considered for Honors).
