merit_note_en: Rutgers–Camden states it will offer scholarships of up to $21,000 to all non-sponsored international applicants who meet admission requirements and enroll full time, with no separate application required and automatic consideration on admission. The award is renewable if the student maintains a 2.5 GPA at Rutgers–Camden, and international students are encouraged to apply by the early action or regular decision due dates because scholarship funds are limited.

name: Texas Christian University
essay_req_en: 1 essay required (300-500 words) — TCU's own application: choose 1 of 4 prompts; Common App, Coalition, and ApplyTexas use that platform's essay (no separate TCU supplement). An optional 'Freedom of Expression' submission (essay, poem, artwork, URL) is recommended.
merit_note_en: TCU states that two types of assistance are available to incoming international students — academic scholarships and need-based financial aid — and that applicants are automatically considered for academic scholarships when they apply for admission. Need-based awards range from $2,000 to $41,570 and require the College Board CSS/Financial Aid PROFILE (TCU code 6820) by February 1 for first-year fall applicants; TCU notes it does not offer full-funding awards.

name: University of Colorado Boulder
essay_req_en: Common App personal essay (250-650 words) + 1 required supplemental short answer (250 words, 'what do you want to study at CU Boulder and why' — must differ from your personal essay). Officially states that applications without essays cannot be reviewed. Confirmed on the 2026-27 cycle page.
merit_note_en: CU Boulder states that international students are eligible for a few merit-based CU Boulder scholarships and that the university cannot provide federal financial aid to international students; it does not accept the College Board International Student Financial Aid Application. Athletic and College of Music scholarships (full or partial) are occasionally available to very talented individuals.

name: Pratt Institute
merit_note_en: All admitted first-year applicants, including international students, are automatically considered for merit scholarships with no separate application; awards for high school applicants are based on GPA and portfolio.

name: Parsons School of Design at The New School
merit_note_en: All admitted Parsons applicants, including international students, are automatically considered for merit scholarships based on the strength of the application and portfolio; no separate application is required. International students are typically eligible only for merit scholarships.

name: Rhode Island School of Design
merit_note_en: RISD states that institutional funding is awarded based on financial need at the time of admission; international applicants are considered by completing the RISD institutional financial aid form in the applicant portal. RISD notes it should not be assumed that aid offers will meet full financial need.

name: California Institute of the Arts
merit_note_en: International students are eligible for select institutional scholarships, typically based on artistic merit as judged from the portfolio, audition and/or writing sample; all applicants are automatically considered with no separate application. CalArts states these funds are limited and competitive and do not cover a student's entire tuition.

name: The Cooper Union for the Advancement of Science and Art
merit_note_en: Cooper Union awards every enrolled undergraduate, domestic and international and in all three schools (art, architecture, engineering), a half-tuition scholarship, currently valued at $22,275 per year. It does not offer separate academic merit scholarships; additional aid is need-based, and international students are not eligible for federal or state aid.

name: School of the Art Institute of Chicago
merit_note_en: International undergraduates are reviewed for SAIC merit scholarships during the admissions process, based on the portfolio, artist's statement and other materials, with no separate application. The Early Action/Priority Merit deadline gives the widest access to merit awards; international students are not eligible for U.S. federal aid.

name: School of Visual Arts
merit_note_en: International students are eligible for the merit-based Silas H. Rhodes Scholarship (first-time freshmen, full-time, minimum 3.0 GPA); there is no separate application, and freshman materials must be submitted by February 1. The Gustave Blache III Art Scholarship (partial tuition, December 1 deadline) is also open to international first-time freshmen.

name: Fashion Institute of Technology
merit_note_en: FIT's financial aid office states that international students are not eligible for financial assistance from FIT; they may only borrow through the Alternative (private) Loan Program, usually with a creditworthy U.S. co-signer. F-1 visa holders are not eligible for the New York State resident tuition rate and pay the out-of-state rate.

name: Maryland Institute College of Art
merit_note_en: MICA's merit-based competitive scholarships recognize artistic talent and academic achievement and are open to students from the United States and abroad; new applicants are considered through the admission application. International students may also submit the CSS Profile to be considered for need-based aid.

name: Savannah College of Art and Design
merit_note_en: Incoming undergraduates, including international students, are automatically reviewed for GPA-based academic scholarships after admission, and those who submit a résumé/list of achievements and/or portfolio are also reviewed for achievement scholarships. The International Student Scholarship requires meeting or exceeding admission requirements and a 500-word essay.

name: Massachusetts College of Art and Design
merit_note_en: International undergraduates may be considered for merit-based scholarships through the admission application but are not eligible for federal aid; MassArt Provost's Scholarships are merit-based awards for accepted first-year and transfer applicants from outside New England, renewable for up to four years. Test scores are not used for merit scholarship consideration.
